intro: The Sila plateau in Calabria holds two very different old-tree visits. Near Camigliatello Silano, I Giganti della Sila is a five-hectare reserve of Corsican pines, 58 of them estimated at more than 350 years old by the FAI, which runs it, and up to 43 metres tall; it is temporarily closed. In the Sila Piccola above Taverna, a free forest track from the Gariglione barracks passes a silver fir over five metres round and a 30-metre beech, both signed by the forest guards.
meta_description: Sila's old trees: the Giganti della Sila pine grove, 350 years and up to 43 m (temporarily closed), and the signed fir and beech of Gariglione.
question_meta: What are the oldest trees in the Sila? The Giganti della Sila, Corsican pines estimated at over 350 years, near Camigliatello Silano.
question_answer: The oldest trees in the Sila are the Giganti della Sila, a grove of Corsican pines near Camigliatello Silano. The FAI estimates 58 of them at more than 350 years old, and the tallest reach 43 metres. The grove is temporarily closed by the FAI, with no reopening date announced.
question_context: The two visits lie some distance apart on the plateau. I Giganti della Sila stands at about 1,400 metres near Croce di Magara, a few kilometres from Camigliatello Silano. The five hectares became the biogenetic nature reserve I Giganti di Fallistro by ministerial decree on 21 July 1987 and are now cared for by the FAI, the Italian heritage trust. Sources count between 52 and 60 pines, and the Sila National Park gives trunks of 2.5 to 6 metres round and heights of 30 to 43 metres. Visitors photographed the grove in August 2026, but the FAI has since closed it until further notice for extraordinary maintenance. The Gariglione trees, in the Sila Piccola above Taverna, are free to see. The silver fir stands beside the dirt track from the forest barracks towards the 1,759-metre summit, 515 centimetres round and 25 metres tall, and a beech 30 metres tall and 415 centimetres round stands about 170 metres further on. The forest guards put a sign at each, and a car is needed for both places.

faq.q: Is I Giganti della Sila open?
faq.a: Not at the moment. The FAI has closed the grove until further notice for extraordinary maintenance, with no reopening date announced. Check fondoambiente.it before going.

faq.q: Can I see old trees in the Sila while the Giganti are closed?
faq.a: Yes. The silver fir and the beech on the forest track from the Gariglione barracks above Taverna are free to visit and signed by the forest guards.

faq.q: When should I go to Gariglione?
faq.a: October, when the beech turns copper among the firs.

faq.q: Can I get there by public transport?
faq.a: We found none. Both places are reached by car, the grove from Camigliatello Silano and the Gariglione track from the forest barracks.

trees.name: I Giganti della Sila Corsican Pine Grove

location.address: Localita Croce di Magara, Fallistro, Spezzano della Sila (CS)

trees.story:
Fifty-eight pines in one small wood on the Sila plateau are estimated at more than 350 years old, and the tallest reach 43 metres. That is the count the FAI, the Italian heritage trust that runs the reserve, gives for I Giganti della Sila, the giants of the Sila. Other sources put the number between 52 and 60.

They are Corsican pines of the laricio form, the native pine of Calabria's mountains, standing at about 1,400 metres near Croce di Magara, a few kilometres from Camigliatello Silano. According to the Sila National Park, their trunks measure 2.5 to 6 metres round at the base and their heights run from 30 to 43 metres. Italy's national register lists them as a single stand rather than as separate trees, and nobody has named one trunk as the largest.

The five hectares were made a biogenetic nature reserve, I Giganti di Fallistro, by ministerial decree on 21 July 1987, and the FAI now cares for them. A visit normally takes about an hour, on a path among the trunks.

The grove was walked and photographed by visitors as recently as August 2026. FAI has since closed it until further notice for extraordinary maintenance, with no reopening date announced.

official_register.name: Elenco degli alberi monumentali d'Italia (MASAF), sheet 02/I896/CS/18 (insieme omogeneo, no girth or height recorded)

trees.access: Temporarily closed. FAI has closed the grove until further notice for extraordinary maintenance works, with no reopening date announced (notice on its site on 2 November 2026). When open, entry is paid (self-guided 6 euro adults, 3 euro ages 6 to 18 and students, free for FAI members), normally April to November 10:00 to 18:00, November weekends only 10:00 to 14:00, closed in winter except groups. Check fondoambiente.it before going.
trees.transport: By car, about 5 km from Camigliatello Silano to Croce di Magara. No regular public transport.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise the grove by the size of its pines, straight trunks up to 43 metres tall, inside the FAI reserve at Croce di Magara near Fallistro, entered from the FAI gate.
trees.verify_notes: ENSEMBLE: one place to stand, the grove is the destination (5 ha reserve, Riserva Naturale Biogenetica 'I Giganti di Fallistro', ministerial decree DM 426 of 21 July 1987, now managed by FAI). Sources give 52 to 60 trees (FAI English page: 58 specimens estimated over 350 years old). Parco Nazionale della Sila page: girth at base 2.5 to 6 m, height 30 to 43 m across the grove. MASAF sheet 02/I896/CS/18 is a stand ('insieme omogeneo'), no single-tree figures. girth_cm left null because no single trunk is named; no single largest pine identified. ALIVE: iNaturalist research-grade observations of Pinus nigra laricio inside the grove with GPS accuracy 2 to 6 m on 2026-05-25 (obs 365000721), 2026-08-22 (393510683), 2025-07-26 and 2025-05-18; a Commons photo of the FAI entrance by Marcuscalabresus dated 2026-08-20. PIN: kept approximate because the grove covers several hectares (MASAF point 39.32463,16.46717 sits within ~50 m of iNat fixes at 39.32469,16.46679 and 39.32424,16.46663); this is a place pin, not a trunk. ACCESS CAUTION: FAI notice of temporary closure for extraordinary maintenance, on the visit page and the English page on 2026-11-02, no reopening date; the English page also says closed in winter. Writer should state the closure caveat or hold publication until reopening. LEAD: none found for a named single largest pine.

trees.name: Gariglione Silver Fir

location.address: Strada forestale dalla caserma forestale del Gariglione, Taverna (CZ)

trees.story:
On a mountain covered in firs, the forest guards of Monte Gariglione picked out this one and put up a sign beside it. Italy's national register agrees with their choice. It measures the trunk at 515 centimetres round at chest height, with a height of 25 metres.

That girth is the remarkable part. A silver fir usually grows as a straight grey column, and one more than five metres round has been putting on wood for a very long time. A local site that photographed it on the track gives it more than 200 years, without saying how it knows, so treat that as a floor rather than a date. Nobody has published a real age. If you know more, tell us.

The tree stands beside the dirt track that leaves the Gariglione forest barracks and climbs to the summit at 1,759 metres, in the state forest of the Sila National Park, in the Sila Piccola above Taverna. About 170 metres further along the same track is a big beech the guards signed too, so the two make one short walk.

We have found no dated photograph of the fir from recent years. The track is free and open, and you will need a car to reach the barracks.

official_register.name: Elenco degli alberi monumentali d'Italia (MASAF), sheet 15/L070/CZ/18

trees.access: Free. On the dirt track that starts near the Gariglione forest barracks (state forest inside the Parco Nazionale della Sila) and climbs to the summit at 1,759 m; the forest guards put information signs at this fir and the beech.
trees.transport: By car to the Gariglione forest barracks above Taverna, then a short walk up the forest track. No public transport.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the forest guards' information sign beside it and a trunk over 5 metres round, on the track up from the Gariglione forest barracks, before the signed beech.
trees.verify_notes: Register: MASAF 15/L070/CZ/18, 515 cm, 25 m. Second source: Silaonline photographed the 'giant silver fir' on the track from the barracks and gives 25 m and 515 cm at 1.3 m, over 200 years old, in the national list; it says the forest guards chose and signed it. Girth and height match the register exactly, so this may be the same measurement, but the site visit and the sign are independent evidence of location. Age 'over 200 years' is a vague source; not entered as an estimate. RECOGNISE: beside the track from the barracks, with a forest-guard information sign (silaonline); the beech sil_003 stands further along the same track. Parco Sila also lists 'Abeti Gemelli' (6.5 m and 5.1 m girth, 37 and 30 m) at the barracks: a possible bigger lead, not checked, may be the same group as register stand 07/L070. ALIVE: no dated page; silaonline article undated; flag. Context 2026: silaonline reports the Giganti della Sila closure of 2026-07-24 as for safety.

trees.name: Gariglione Beech

location.address: Strada forestale dalla caserma forestale del Gariglione, Taverna (CZ)

trees.story:
A beech the height of a ten-storey building stands beside the forest track on Monte Gariglione, and it has the numbers to prove it. In June 2016 a local Sila site measured it at 30 metres tall and 413 centimetres round at chest height. Italy's national register gives 415. Two centimetres apart, which is about as close as two measurements of a living tree ever get.

The forest guards marked it with an information sign, as they did the giant silver fir about 170 metres back down the same track. The track starts at the Gariglione forest barracks and climbs through the state forest of the Sila National Park towards the summit at 1,759 metres, in the Sila Piccola above Taverna.

The same local site says the beech is more than 200 years old, but gives no basis, so we leave the age open. If you know when it started, tell us.

Our most recent record of it is that 2016 measurement, so a dated photograph from a visitor would be welcome. In October the beech turns copper and gold among the dark firs, which is the best reason to make the drive.

official_register.name: Elenco degli alberi monumentali d'Italia (MASAF), sheet 10/L070/CZ/18

trees.access: Free. Same dirt track as sil_002, from the Gariglione forest barracks toward the summit; signed by the forest guards.
trees.transport: By car to the Gariglione forest barracks above Taverna, then a walk of a few minutes up the forest track. No public transport.

best_time.label: October, when the beech turns copper among the firs

trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the forest guards' sign beside a tall grey beech, 30 metres high and over 4 metres round, on the track from the Gariglione barracks about 170 metres past the signed fir.
trees.verify_notes: Register: MASAF 10/L070/CZ/18, 415 cm, 30 m. Silaonline: beech in the national list, measured June 2016 at 30 m and 413 cm at 1.3 m, over 200 years old, photographed on the track and signed by the forest guards. RECOGNISE: roadside beech with a guard sign on the track from the barracks. Roughly 170 m from sil_002; the two could be one outing. ALIVE: measured 2016 per silaonline; no newer dated record; flag. Age not entered.
